editions.title: Signal · Friday 13 November
editions.overview: Jensen Huang leaves Nvidia with immediate effect, the finance ministry fines former Credit Suisse chair Urs Rohner, and wealth platform FNZ pulls back to its core markets.

editions.title: Signal · Thursday 12 November
editions.overview: McKinsey finds Swiss banks highly profitable but short of AI scale, Nvidia's board weighs Jensen Huang's future, and the SNB sees no credit crunch.

editions.title: Signal · Wednesday 11 November
editions.overview: Anthropic sets the price range for its IPO, global banks put about USD 270 million behind a joint stablecoin, and Avaloq takes its Mosaic platform to the US.

editions.title: Signal · Tuesday 10 November
editions.overview: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 at a lower price, Crédit Agricole proposes merging Banco BPM with its Italian arm, and Evident counts a record 111 new AI use cases at banks in the third quarter.

editions.title: Signal · Monday 9 November
editions.overview: Nvidia's board opens an investigation after reports its chief executive was targeted by foreign intelligence, Anthropic's IPO talk falls to about USD 1.2 trillion as OpenAI raises at USD 1.25 trillion, and South Korea moves to scrap bank network separation rules after AI-assisted hacks.

editions.title: Signal · Sunday 8 November
editions.overview: The UBS capital fight turns to a compromise idea, banks put numbers on AI, Binance traces its theft to a tampered AI tool, rates rise as AI stocks fall, and supervisors start inspecting bank AI.

editions.title: Signal · Friday 6 November
editions.overview: An AI-led rout wipes USD 2.5 trillion from US stocks and reaches Asia, Claude starts reading US bank accounts through Plaid, and China blocks SoftBank's purchase of ABB's robotics division.

editions.title: Signal · Thursday 5 November
editions.overview: The OCC's AI framework for US bank examiners, a reported valuation compromise in the UBS capital dispute and the markets' reaction to the Democrats' sweep of Congress lead this morning.

editions.title: Signal · Wednesday 4 November
editions.overview: FINMA's chair unveils an AI pilot running on the authority's own hardware, Binance traces its USD 6.3 billion theft to a fake job interview and AI tooling, and an EU court adviser says chatbots can infringe press publishers' rights.

editions.title: Signal · Tuesday 3 November
editions.overview: Goldman Sachs limits AI coding tools to engineers, Swiss cantonal banks warn against a FINMA 'mega authority', and Anthropic's amended filing says it may imminently meet its AI-acceleration threshold.

editions.title: Signal · Sunday 1 November
editions.overview: UBS beats on profit as its capital fight with Bern hardens, the Federal Council sets a timetable for binding AI rules, banks put AI agents to work, the AI labs raise big numbers and hard questions, and a record Binance theft meets AI-run attacks.

editions.title: Signal · Saturday 31 October
editions.overview: Euro area supervisors put generative AI use at about 85 percent of banks, Bern finds a UBS move abroad would bring little capital relief, and North Korean hackers are blamed for a record theft from Binance.

editions.title: Signal · Friday 30 October
editions.overview: The ECB holds rates as energy pushes inflation to 3.8 percent, BBVA puts AI agents at the centre of a strong quarter, and Société Générale posts a record third quarter.

editions.title: Signal · Thursday 29 October
editions.overview: Bern sets out its path to binding AI rules, Swiss banks stay loyal to core systems they rate poorly on AI, and Canada's big banks shut out personal AI agents.
